title: NEXORA SubscriptionSource
description: A subscription feed that yields Servers. Fetch semantics mirror the already-correct legacy path (fetch -> sha256 -> compare -> keep-last-good, docs/audit/09) and add the durable status the legacy path lacks, so a background refresh failure is still visible days later.

id.description: UUID v4 identity; the envelope key is -nexora.subscription.<id> and Servers point back at it.

displayName.description: Label shown in the Subscriptions list. Not an identifier.

url.description: https only, and no userinfo: a credential-bearing URL would be stored and synced in clear. Also no credential in the query: feeds routinely ship '?token=...', which is a secret wearing the shape of an address, so a token-bearing address belongs in urlRef and this field carries the display form -- scheme, host, path, query dropped (docs/architecture/29 §4). SSRF guard (loopback/link-local/metadata rejection) is a Connector-side control, not a schema property -- see docs/architecture/29 and SEC-2.

headersRef.description: Authorization and similar headers are keystore references. Inline headers is exactly the SEC-1 leak path (omega-target/src/options.coffee:27).

format.description: Parser selection, declared rather than sniffed: an ambiguous body must fail rather than guess a transport.

limits.description: Ceilings enforced before the body is parsed. The legacy loader has none (docs/audit/11 SEC-2).

keepLastGood.description: A failed refresh MUST NOT delete the last working version. Fixed to true: it is not a user preference.

schedule.description: When refresh runs and how backoff grows after failures.

status.description: Persisted, not transient. The legacy engine computes this information and throws it away (docs/audit/09).

serverIds.description: Servers produced by the last successful parse. Owned by the refresh, so user edits to them are expected to be lost; manual changes belong on a copy.

createdAt.description: First successful or attempted import of this source.

updatedAt.description: Last change to the source document itself, not to the servers it produced.

urlRef.description: Keystore reference holding the FULL fetch address when it carries a credential in its query or path. 'url' then holds the display form -- scheme, host and path with the query dropped -- which is what the UI shows and what sync carries. Optional: a feed whose address is not secret uses 'url' alone. Chosen per-source rather than by sniffing, because the schema cannot tell a token from a tracking parameter (docs/architecture/29 §4, ADR-0010).

allOf.description: A credential in the query string is the SEC-1 leak wearing a different hat: `Authorization` had a schema field of its own, `?token=` had none, and this namespace is sync-eligible, so an unsanitised token would travel to the browser account, the Gist and the WebDAV target. A `urlRef` therefore has to exist whenever the address carries a credential-shaped parameter; `url` keeps the display form. First-letter case classes are spelled out because JSON Schema patterns are case-sensitive -- the Connector re-checks case-insensitively at fetch time (docs/architecture/29 §4, docs/architecture/31).
